title: Measuring a Ticket's Trip Charges: Change, Bag and Upgrade Charges
content:
**Revenue accounting definition — Crestline Tickets by Fare Brand.** The trip charges of a ticket are its change, bag and upgrade charges, measured by one of three conventions:

| Ticket | Trip charges |
|---|---|
| At least one flown coupon | The change, bag and upgrade charges recorded against the first unflown segment plus the itinerary-level charges recorded against no segment |
| Round trip with no flown coupon | Half of every change, bag and upgrade charge on the ticket |
| Any other ticket | Every change, bag and upgrade charge on the ticket |

Change charges include change fees and same-day change fees; bag charges include bag charges by count and weight or size charges; upgrade charges are paid upgrade purchases. A change fee is recorded at the itinerary level, against no segment.

## Worked cases (hypothetical)

| Ticket | Charges on the ticket | Trip charges |
|---|---|---|
| Two segments, segment 1 flown | Change fee 100.00 (itinerary level); bag 35.00 on segment 1; bag 45.00 on segment 2 | 145.00 |
| Round trip, nothing flown | Change fee 100.00; bags 35.00 and 45.00 | 90.00 |
| One way, nothing flown | Bag 35.00; weight charge 100.00 | 135.00 |
